title: Hello World Python Script
problem_statement: The user needs a minimal Python script that prints 'Hello World' to standard output, serving as a basic program entry point or a smoke test to verify the Python runtime environment.
target_users: Anyone needing a minimal executable Python template

functional_requirements.description: Create a Python source file named hello.py
acceptance_criteria: A file named hello.py exists in the expected directory
The file is a plain text file with valid Python syntax
The file contains only the expected print statement and no extraneous code

functional_requirements.description: Print the exact string 'Hello World' to standard output when executed
acceptance_criteria: Running 'python hello.py' outputs exactly 'Hello World' followed by a newline
No error messages are written to stderr

non_functional_requirements.description: Script must execute in under 1 second on any standard Python interpreter
The file must be readable and directly runnable without modification
The script must run on any Python 3.x interpreter without version-specific issues

constraints: Python 3.x must be installed on the target system
The file must use only the Python standard library (no external dependencies)
assumptions: The user has a working Python 3.x installation accessible from the command line
The output target is standard output (stdout), not a file or other destination
The casing of 'Hello World' is intentional (camel case with capital H and W, no punctuation)

clarifying_questions.question: Should the output be exactly 'Hello World' (without exclamation mark or other punctuation), or should it include '!' as in the traditional 'Hello World!'?
Should the script use a shebang line (#!/usr/bin/env python3) for direct execution on Unix systems?
